answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token before it can post bids, with slashing for proven fraud. A newcomer may earn trust slowly through small jobs, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every extra identity ties up more capital, and dishonest behavior risks losing it. The ember, tundra, and sparrow agents all face the same collateral rule; names are free, but economic weight is not. This raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the influence they seek.
